answers.question: Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?
answers.answer: No, please do not add the two missed runs on top of this week. After a fever and with a cough still hanging on, piling on extra sessions is the fastest way to get sick again or pick up a niggle. Three runs at the usual spacing is the right dose. You have eight weeks to the race, which is plenty of time to catch up by building steadily, one week at a time.

new.analysis:
## Why this week looks like this

The one priority is to come back from illness without a setback, because a fever on Wednesday night is very recent and you are still coughing. We are repeating a familiar walk-run pattern, not stacking the missed sessions on top.

Monday is a shorter check-in run so you can read how your body responds. If breathing feels normal and the cough stays above the neck, Wednesday matches what you did two weeks ago, and Saturday nudges a little longer. If anything feels worse during a run, walk the rest and stop.

You still have eight weeks until Corrowmore, which is plenty of runway for a first 5K. Missing two runs to illness does not cost you the race; trying to make them up this week could. We will add volume again next week once you have strung three clean sessions together.

## How to run the sessions

Keep the run portions at a pace where you could speak a short sentence. The walk portions are brisk, not a stroll, and the shoes stay the New Balance 880s you have been using.

safetyCallouts.title: Returning to running after a fever.
safetyCallouts.body: You had a fever as recently as Thursday night and are still coughing and congested. If the cough sits in your chest, you feel breathless at rest, your heart races, or the fever comes back, skip the run and see your GP before training again. Keep efforts easy this week and stop any session that feels worse than it started.
